title: The Heart
question: Which chamber is glowing?
lines: Can you name the chamber that's glowing?
This is a human heart, seen from the front.
Which chamber is lit up?
Careful: the heart's left side is on your right.
Its wall is the thickest in the heart.
It's A. The left ventricle.
Why it matters: it pumps blood out to your whole body.

title: The Heart
question: Which chamber is glowing?
lines: Blood from your whole body enters here first. Name it.
Watch the chamber that's glowing.
Which chamber is it?
Oxygen-poor blood comes back through two big veins.
They empty into this upper chamber on the heart's right.
It's C. The right atrium.
Why it matters: your heart's natural pacemaker sits in its wall.

title: The Heart
question: Which blood vessel is it?
lines: Is this glowing tube the aorta? Look closer.
It sits right at the top of the heart.
Which blood vessel is it?
It leaves the right ventricle, not the left.
It carries blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen.
It's B. The pulmonary trunk.
Why it matters: it's an artery that carries oxygen-poor blood.
